issues.legal_issue: For a usufructuary mortgage, the limitation period for recovering possession does not begin merely when the mortgage is created, but when the mortgagor’s right to recover possession accrues under the mortgage arrangement.
material_facts: The mortgage transferred possession to the mortgagee, who was entitled to retain possession and apply the property’s rents and profits toward the mortgage debt.
The mortgage fixed no time for repayment or redemption.

The mortgagee sought to establish ownership after the property had remained unredeemed for more than sixty years, but the relevant repayment or balance-payment event under the mortgage had not occurred.
issues.conclusion: The limitation period does not begin until the mortgage money is paid from the rents and profits, or, where only part is discharged from those proceeds, until the mortgagor pays, tenders, or deposits the remaining balance as applicable. The passage of time from the creation of the mortgage alone does not extinguish the mortgagor’s right to recover possession.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 58(d) and 62 of the Transfer of Property Act distinguish a usufructuary mortgage and its special right to recover possession from other mortgages; Section 62 provides when that right accrues. Article 61 of the Limitation Act measures limitation from accrual of the right to redeem or recover possession, not automatically from the mortgage date. The Court relied on Seth Ganga Dhar v. Shankar Lal, Harbans v. Om Prakash, Prithi Nath Singh v. Suraj Ahir, Jayasingh Dhyanu Mhoprekar v. Krishna Babaji Patil, and Panchanan Sharma v. Basudeo Prasad Jaganani. It rejected the contrary observation in Prabhakaran v. M. Azhagiri Pillai and distinguished Sampuran Singh v. Niranjan Kaur because that case did not concern a usufructuary mortgage.

rule.if: usufructuary_mortgage_proceeding and mortgagee_receives_rents_or_profits and not possession_right_triggered

predicates.usufructuary_mortgage_proceeding: The dispute concerns a mortgage under which possession was delivered or promised to the mortgagee, who was authorized to receive rents or profits from the property.
predicates.mortgagee_receives_rents_or_profits: The mortgagee retains possession and is entitled to apply the property’s rents or profits toward interest or repayment of the mortgage debt.
predicates.possession_right_triggered: The mortgage debt has been discharged from rents or profits, or any required remaining balance has been paid, tendered, or deposited by the mortgagor.
predicates.limitation_period_has_not_started: The limitation period for the mortgagor’s recovery of possession has not begun.

issues.definition: When a usufructuary mortgagee receives rents or profits and the mortgagor’s right to recover possession has not yet been triggered, the limitation period for recovery of possession has not started.

issues.legal_issue: A usufructuary mortgagee cannot acquire absolute ownership merely because the mortgagor has not redeemed the mortgage within the limitation period measured from the mortgage’s creation.
material_facts: The mortgagee remained in possession under a usufructuary mortgage.
The mortgagee sought a declaration of ownership based on the property having remained unredeemed for more than sixty years.
The mortgagor’s right had not been extinguished by an act of the parties or a court decree.
issues.conclusion: A usufructuary mortgagee is not entitled to a declaration of ownership merely on the expiry of thirty years from the date of the mortgage; a unilateral claim of ownership does not extinguish the mortgagor’s right.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, the right to redeem subsists unless extinguished by an act of the parties or a court decree; Section 62 specifies the usufructuary mortgagor’s right to recover possession. Article 61 of the Limitation Act runs from accrual of that right, as specified by Section 62, rather than automatically from the mortgage date. The Court applied the principle that once a mortgage, always a mortgage, relying on Jayasingh Dhyanu Mhoprekar v. Krishna Babaji Patil, Parichhan Mistry v. Acchiabar Mistry, and Hamzabi v. Syed Karimuddin, among other authorities.

predicates.usufructuary_mortgagee_ownership_claim: A mortgagee under a usufructuary mortgage seeks a declaration that the mortgaged property is absolutely owned by the mortgagee.
predicates.claim_based_only_on_elapsed_time: The mortgagee bases the ownership claim only on the passage of time without redemption.
predicates.no_lawful_extinguishment: No act of the parties or court decree has extinguished the mortgagor’s right to redeem or recover possession.
predicates.mortgagee_cannot_claim_absolute_ownershi: The mortgagee cannot claim absolute ownership on the asserted basis.

issues.definition: When a usufructuary mortgagee bases an ownership claim only on elapsed time and the mortgagor’s right has not been lawfully extinguished, the mortgagee cannot claim absolute ownership.
